blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, the balance between direct and indirect taxes is itself a strategic variable. Direct taxes — corporate and income tax — hit the company's profitability visibly. Indirect taxes — VAT, duties, levies — hit the customer through the price, but shape the company's operations quietly. A business where indirect taxes dominate is a business whose customers feel the government's presence more than its shareholders do.

Rarely do senior leaders treat this balance as a choice. They should. A change in pricing structure, a shift in sourcing location, a new legal entity in a different jurisdiction — each moves the balance between direct and indirect exposure in ways that change how the company actually competes.

The best executives ask not only how much tax, but also which kind. The answer reveals something the P&L alone never does: who, in the end, is really paying the tax burden — and whether that is the right answer for where the business is trying to go.

items.q: According to the text, how do direct and indirect taxes differ in their visibility?
options: Both are equally visible on the P&L
Direct taxes hit profitability visibly, while indirect taxes shape operations quietly
Indirect taxes are the only ones that appear in the accounts
Direct taxes are hidden inside the price paid by customers
items.why: "Direct taxes… hit the company's profitability visibly. Indirect taxes… shape the company's operations quietly."

items.q: What does the text say about how senior leaders usually treat the direct/indirect balance?
options: They rarely treat it as a choice
They optimise it every quarter
They delegate it entirely to auditors
They regard it as the single most important decision
items.why: "Rarely do senior leaders treat this balance as a choice. They should."

items.q: The author suggests that a business dominated by indirect taxes is one in which…
options: shareholders bear the entire burden directly
customers feel the government's presence more than shareholders do
no tax burden reaches the customer at all
profitability is always higher than average
items.why: Inferência apoiada no texto: se o imposto indireto domina, ele recai sobre o cliente via preço, não sobre o acionista.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The kind of tax a company bears is strategically as important as the amount
Choosing where to source or incorporate shifts a company's tax exposure
The P&L alone tells you everything about who really pays the tax burden
Pricing decisions can quietly alter the direct/indirect balance
items.why: Inferência: o texto afirma que a resposta 'revela algo que o P&L sozinho nunca revela' — logo o autor discordaria de que o P&L basta.

items.q: The final paragraph implies that the question "which kind of tax?" matters because it…
options: reduces the total tax paid in every case
exposes who ultimately bears the burden and whether that fits the strategy
is required by law in most jurisdictions
simplifies the company's reporting obligations
items.why: Inferência: a pergunta revela 'who is really paying the tax burden — and whether that is the right answer for where the business is trying to go'.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry apresentando a revisão à diretoria. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you. Before I take you through the numbers, let me be clear about what this review is and is not. It is not a warning that we are paying too much tax overall. Our headline rate is unchanged. What it is, is a picture of a shift in the kind of tax we carry — and that shift has gone completely unnoticed.

Over the last three years, our indirect tax exposure — VAT, duties, the levies attached to certain sourcing routes — has tripled. Not risen. Tripled. And because none of that lands on the profitability line, the board never saw it. It was invisible in the P&L.

Now, some of you will ask why this matters if the cash eventually washes through. It matters because the timing does not. Indirect tax ties up working capital months before we recover it, and on the volumes we now trade, that is real money sitting idle.

My recommendation is not to reverse anything overnight. It is to treat this balance as a decision from here on — every new sourcing location, every pricing change, reviewed for what it does to the mix. Manage it, and it becomes a lever. Ignore it, and it manages us.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Harry say this review is NOT about?
options: A warning that the company is paying too much tax overall
A change in the kind of tax the company carries
The company's indirect tax exposure
The timing of cash recovery
items.why: "It is not a warning that we are paying too much tax overall. Our headline rate is unchanged."

items.q: By how much has the indirect tax exposure changed over three years?
options: It has doubled
It has tripled
It has stayed flat
It has fallen slightly
items.why: "our indirect tax exposure… has tripled. Not risen. Tripled."

items.q: Why did the board never notice the shift, according to Harry?
options: The figures were deliberately hidden by management
It did not land on the profitability line, so it was invisible in the P&L
The auditors failed to report it
It happened too quickly to measure
items.why: "because none of that lands on the profitability line, the board never saw it. It was invisible in the P&L."

items.q: When someone asks why it matters if the cash eventually washes through, what is Harry's implied point?
options: The total amount of tax is actually higher than reported
The timing hurts — indirect tax ties up working capital before it is recovered
The cash never washes through at all
The board should not concern itself with cash flow
items.why: Inferência: "It matters because the timing does not" — o capital de giro fica preso meses antes da recuperação.

items.q: What does Harry mean by "Manage it, and it becomes a lever. Ignore it, and it manages us"?
options: The exposure should be eliminated immediately
Controlled deliberately it is a strategic tool; left alone it will dictate the company's choices
The board should stop trading in high-levy routes entirely
Only the finance team can influence the outcome
items.why: Inferência: tratar o balanço como decisão o transforma em alavanca; ignorá-lo deixa que ele controle a empresa.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Leadership finally treated the direct/indirect mix as a genuine strategic variable." A strategic variable is…
options: a factor leaders can deliberately adjust to shape the company's position
a fixed cost that cannot be altered
an accounting error found during the audit
a legal obligation set entirely by regulators
items.why: Strategic variable = variável estratégica: algo que a liderança pode ajustar para mudar a posição do negócio.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Corporate tax reduces reported ___ directly, whereas VAT does not."
options: profitability
sourcing
recovery
jurisdiction
items.why: Profitability = lucratividade: é o que o imposto direto reduz visivelmente.

items.q: "A new import duty raised the landed cost of every shipment from that region." A duty here is…
options: a tax charged on imported goods
a moral obligation of the trader
a discount granted at the port
a shareholder dividend
items.why: Duty = imposto de importação, cobrado sobre a mercadoria que entra.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Shifting our ___ from one country to another altered both the duties we paid and our tax residence."
options: sourcing location
pricing structure
tax burden
headline rate
items.why: Sourcing location = local de suprimento: mudá-lo altera impostos de importação e residência fiscal.

items.q: "On these volumes, our indirect tax exposure has become material." Exposure means…
options: the extent to which the company is subject to that liability or risk
the public disclosure of the accounts
the time spent negotiating with regulators
the profit margin on each trade
items.why: Exposure = exposição: o grau em que a empresa está sujeita àquela obrigação ou risco.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de estratégia tributária. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the new entity in Singapore." To sign off on means to…
options: formally approve
quietly ignore
audit in detail
postpone indefinitely
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on reopening the sourcing route." They…
options: resisted or objected to it
approved it at once
delegated it to finance
signed it without reading
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed to review the mix quarterly, but the team never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
finished it ahead of schedule
documented it thoroughly
escalated it to the board
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "Trimming a few basis points off the headline rate will not move the needle on our real exposure." This means it will…
options: not make a noticeable difference
provoke immediate resistance
breach the reporting rules
take years to calculate
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "This shift had been flying under the radar for three years." It had been…
options: going unnoticed by those in charge
openly debated in every meeting
formally reported each quarter
blocked by the regulator
items.why: Fly under the radar = passar despercebido, sem chamar atenção — como a exposição indireta invisível no P&L.
